newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bond yields ease, longs eye tender.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bond yields ease, longs eye tender.

text.p: *Australian bond yields edged lower during a slow trading session with sentiment remaining bolstered by the possibilty of a domestic interest rate cut in the near future.

Australian bond yields edged lower during a slow trading session with sentiment remaining bolstered by the possibility of a domestic interest rate cut in the near future, combined with a firm U.S. bond market, traders said.

However, the long end slightly underperformed short dated maturities ahead of Tuesday's A$800 million two-tranche Treasury bond tender, which includes A$600 million in a new line of 7.5 percent September 2009 stock.
"There's some concern over the size of the new stock. But I'm reasonable positive on the outcome of the tender. I'm positive on the market overall," one trader said.

Short maturities were also supported by swap activity related to at least one dual currency samuari bond issue. The Canadian province of Ontario was confirmed as issuing a 30 billion yen transaction under this structure.
This business was also one of the reasons which propelled the Australian dollar to its highest level against the yen in more than four years and through 90 yen.

Meanwhile, there is no local data until the release of the September balance of paymenets on Wednesday, which is expected to see the current account deficit at A$1.3 billion and little changed from the August result.

The local market slightly underperformed the U.S. market, which sees key data for GDP and payrolls this week. However, it continued to outperform Canadian debt, which weakened during an illiquid session on Friday. The New Zealand market was closed for Labour Day today.
